subject: Mediapulse — evaluation next steps: model recommendations, fn-call & JSON schema plan
messages:
From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.example>

Cc: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.example>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.example>, soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.example>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery follow-up — Mediapulse evaluation: model fit, fn-call & schema plan

Hi Ella — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we can turn the conversation into an actionable evaluation: 

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary workflows: ad creative summarization + structured ad-performance record generation for downstream analytics.
- SLAs: 200ms median token latency for inference in production; batch up to 16 req/sec during peak.
- Quality concern: accuracy of numeric fields (CTR, spend) and consistent JSON schema conformance across retries.

Redwood's proposed evaluation focus
1) Model-fit candidates (shortlist for tests):
   - Mistral-Instruct-7B (fast, cost-efficient baseline)
   - Llama-2-13B-qa-8bit (midpoint: better instruction following for numerical extraction)
   - Falcon-40B-instruct-quant (higher-quality candidate if accuracy needs spike)

2) Tests we want to run (deliverables)
   - Benchmark workbook: throughput/latency & per-field accuracy (we'll populate first tab).
   - Prompt set v1 (attached): ~250 representative prompts spanning canonical/edge cases.
   - JSON schema conformance suite: schema for ad-performance objects + failure/retry signals.
   - Fn-call (tool) integration test: function signature in the request to return structured object; end-to-end parsing & idempotency checks.

3) Reliability & retry guidance (proposal)
   - Client: 3 retries on 5xx with exponential backoff (200ms -> 600ms -> 1800ms) + full jitter; ensure idempotency keys for write-paths.
   - Server: we'll run a canary with 1% of traffic pinned to highest-quality model and compare schema error rate.

Ask from you
- Sample dataset (CSV or NDJSON) with 500 rows (anonymized) so we can seed prompts and measure numeric extraction accuracy.
- Shortlist of 2–3 APIs that will consume the structured output (helps shape schema).
- Confirmation on whether SSO/KMS is needed for sandbox access.

Timeline (proposed)
- Week 0 (this week): we exchange data and Redwood shares benchmark + prompt sets.
- Week 1: smoke runs across the three model candidates, schema tests and basic fn-call semantics.
- Week 2: extended regression (2–3k requests) + latency/throughput tuning.

I'll attach the first pass of the prompt set and a benchmark workbook tonight. If that plan looks good, Monica will coordinate the evaluation window.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Hi Ella — thanks for the quick reply and for the sample. Answers inline + attachments + an explicit test plan.

Security/SOC2 + logs
- Redwood provides SOC2 Type II evidence and can enable forwarding of request/response logs to your SIEM via secure syslog or an S3 sink with encryption at rest. We'll include a SOC2 pack and a templated logging policy in the Drive link.

Schema validation & retries (how we'll handle missing fields)
- We will run a JSON schema validator as a post-response hook in the eval run. Any schema violation gets recorded as a failure in the benchmark workbook (error type + model + input id).
- Our eval harness will re-run problematic cases up to 2 times with a different temperature/prompt fallback. For production we recommend 3 client-side retries for transient server errors; for schema mis-parses we recommend: 1 automated model fallback (lower temperature, more explicit schema prompt) + emission of a validation flag so downstream systems can decide to queue or drop.

Cost & pilot estimate (rough)
- 2-week pilot (smoke + regression): estimated $4k–$8k depending on the volume of regression runs and which model variant we pin for dedicated slots.
- If you want a dedicated reserved GPU window for a 48-hour stress run, we will provide a short-term reserved pool for an additional one-time fee (we'll surface exact numbers in the formal quote).

Attached: mediapulse-benchmark.xlsx (workbook with tabs: plan, latency-targets, error taxonomy) and the prompt-sets file referenced earlier.

Proposed concrete next steps
- Monica: set up sandbox credentials (KMS + IP allowlist) once Ella confirms SSO requirement.
- Soojin: run initial schema conformance tests on the 500-row sample and report per-field precision/recall.
- Me (Karthik): collect any licensing / procurement contacts and get the pilot quote over.

Can we target a kickoff on Thursday (Dec 3) to start smoke runs if we have data by Wednesday EOD?

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Looping back with the internal action plan after reviewing the sample and the attachments: 

Short plan (internal)
- Day 0 (Wed): ingest Mediapulse 500-row NDJSON into our eval harness; run schema validator against the attached schema.
- Day 1 (Thu): smoke runs across the three candidate models. Metrics: field-level F1 for numeric fields, schema-error-rate, median token latency.
- Day 2–3 (Fri–Mon): extended regression with 3k synthetic + real-hybrid requests. We'll pin Llama-2-13B-qa-8bit for the mid test and Falcon-40B-instruct-quant for the quality bucket.

Operational asks
- Need approval: reserve a dedicated 48-hour capacity window (GPU reservation) for the stress run — estimated cost $1,200.
- KMS + IP allowlist details from Ella — Monica, please confirm SSO vs service-account flow.

Deliverables to Ella by Mon morning
- Filled benchmark workbook (first-pass numbers), a short runbook describing retry behavior, and a summary of model-recommendations with tradeoffs.

I'll create a calendar invite for Thursday kickoff (30 min) and include a short Drilldown doc for the CS/infra teams. If budget approval is needed, Karhik please confirm the go-ahead to bill the pilot estimate to the deal.

Thanks,
Soojin
